column15: Confirmed genuine Blended Scotch Whisky (legally must be Scotland-made) via two retailer/export pages opened this session; sold through multiple unrelated négociants (SLAUR SARDET/France among others, also seen via Uruguay/Maldives retailers) with no single identifiable trademark owner, so owner left blank. No smoky or Islay branding found anywhere; peat corrected from unknown to none as an ordinary blend, country corrected from XX to GB-SCT.

Peat corrected from none to light: Arran's own site states the Robert Burns Blend carries "a subtle hint of peat smoke" alongside Arran single malt at its heart. Officially endorsed by the Robert Burns World Federation since 1998 (the only distillery permitted to use his name/signature). Arran also sells a separate Robert Burns single malt (unpeated) -- if the catalogue actually scrapes that product rather than the blend, peat should revert to none; flagged for reviewer to confirm which one this row represents. Added parentSlug=arran.

Confirmed as a genuine Sazerac Company Canadian whisky brand, barrels selected by Sazerac's own master blender; country Canada per the product's own listing. No peat/smoke mentioned; Canadian whisky is essentially never peated, category default retained but now backed by a real, confirmed brand.

Real product confirmed to exist via multiple Ukrainian retail listings (rozetka.com.ua, winestore.com.ua, magtorg.org.ua, gradus.market) describing an aged blended/grain whisky, apparently part of a "St Bernard dog"-themed own-label family alongside the similarly branded "Barry Bernard" (also Ukraine-market, per packagingoftheworld.com) and "Glant Bernard" seen in the same search results. Every specific product page attempted this session errored (500/404/403) or returned no usable detail, so producer, precise country and peat remain unconfirmed -- kept low.

column7: Sakurao Brewery and Distillery Co., Ltd
column15: Confirmed via the distillery's own official site (Hatsukaichi, Hiroshima Prefecture; distilling since Oct. 2018). Range spans a "Sakurao" single malt, "Togouchi" blended whisky and gin, so defaultTypeName left empty. The single malt's finish is described on the official site as "smoky, barrel fragrance," attributed to cask character rather than a peating statement. Withheld peat proposal: light, per third-party reviews (wordsofwhisky.com, uisuki.com, jpwhisky.net) calling the single malt lightly peated -- no producer-domain statement of peated malt found this session, so kept unknown per the strict rule.

Confirmed via scotchwhisky.com as a genuine, now-discontinued private-label blend made at Loch Lomond distillery and bottled at Glen Catrine during Sandy Bulloch's tenure, for the Italian market. No peat/smoke stated; treated as an ordinary own-label blend per the documented-unpeated allowance.

Confirmed as a genuine Duncan Taylor (independent bottler, Huntly, Aberdeenshire) blended Scotch brand, listed directly on scotchwhisky.com's Duncan Taylor company page. Three-year-old value blend; no peat/smoke character described, ordinary-blend default applied.

Confirmed via a consumer review as a genuine blended Scotch whisky (grain + malt spirits, minimum 3 years, 40% ABV) with a Speyside-themed brand story, marketed mainly to the Russian market. Single-source evidence only (a review blog, not a trade reference) -- no specific bottling company identified. No peat/smoke mentioned; ordinary-blend default applied.

Corrected countryCode from GB-ENG to CA. It is a "100% Canadian Rye Whisky" (3-year-old, 40% ABV) named for a Prohibition-era Quebec lodge/blender who sold liquor to American visitors -- unrelated to the English town of Shefford (Bedfordshire) the seed guessed from the name alone. No distillery/company name found across several retailer listings tried. No peat; Canadian whisky category default applied.

Confirmed via Michter's own official site. Part of Michter's annual Legacy Series (since 2018), honoring the 1753 Shenk's distillery that eventually became Michter's; a Kentucky sour mash whiskey (91.2 proof, distinct from bourbon per the source). defaultTypeName left empty since sour mash is not in the closed list. No peat. parentSlug=michters kept from seed (live).

Confirmed via the company's own product page: Shinobu Distillery / Shin Group, Niigata Prefecture, Japan. "The Shin Blended Whisky" is 50% malted barley / 50% grain, finished in Mizunara oak. No peat/smoke stated on the official page -- kept unknown rather than none since no explicit unpeated statement was found. Same company/cluster as the "Shinobu"-branded lines referenced in the seed's note.

Identified via two Ukrainian retail listings as "Sir Park Single Malt," France, produced by Distillerie Tessendier & Fils SAS -- the Cognac house behind Park Cognac (named for Scot Dominique Park), the already-live "Arlett" French whisky and Seven Yards Scotch Whisky. Not currently listed on Tessendier's own spirits page (distillerie-tessendier.com/spirits), so possibly an older or export-only line -- noted, not disqualifying. Kind corrected from blend to brand (single malt, not a multi-source blend). Confirms the seed's "Sir Edward's-style French naming pattern" guess, though from a different producer. No smoke/peat mentioned.

Confirmed via the official site: a licensed collaboration between the band Slipknot and Cedar Ridge Distillery (Iowa's first licensed distillery since Prohibition), a blend of straight rye and straight bourbon mashed/distilled/aged in Iowa. defaultTypeName left empty (spans rye and bourbon, no single closed-list value fits). No peat.

Corrected countryCode from XX to GB-SCT and peat from unknown to heavy. Confirmed via Angus Dundee's own official product page as an Islay Blended Malt Scotch Whisky (46% ABV) -- "rich aromas of fireside soot and coastal smokehouses," "exquisite balance of smoke and peppery spice." Satisfies both auto-gate corroboration paths (producer's own domain and Islay). Angus Dundee (owner of Tomintoul and Glencadam, neither on Islay) sources/blends the Islay malts for this line rather than distilling them itself.

Confirmed via Pernod Ricard's own official brand page: West Virginia craft distillery (Greenbrier Valley), part of Pernod Ricard since 2016. Makes wheated and rye bourbons (Old Scout, Contradiction, Founders') -- range spans types so defaultTypeName stays empty. No peat (standard American whiskey); replaces the seed's generic Wikipedia citations with a direct owner confirmation.

Corrected countryCode from XX to GB-SCT and kind from blend to brand. Spearhead is an unconventional single grain Scotch whisky (100% malted barley through a Coffey still) from Loch Lomond Distillery, finished in toasted virgin oak barrels -- a single-distillery product, not a blend of multiple sources. No peat/smoke mentioned.

Corrected the withheld peat proposal from "likely none" to "likely light": scotchwhisky.com confirms Spice King blends about 16 distillery characters including Islay malts that "impart a slightly salty and smoky finish," and independent reviews (drinkhacker.com, scotchnoob.com) agree there is a genuine, if subtle, peated component behind the dominant spice character. Kept peatProfile=unknown per the strict rule -- wemyssmalts.com could not be reached this session (SSL handshake failure), so no producer-domain confirmation of the positive claim was obtained. defaultTypeName corrected from empty to malt (Blended Malt Scotch Whisky).

Corrected kind from blend to brand and defaultTypeName from empty to bourbon: confirmed as a genuine Kentucky Straight Bourbon Whiskey (~$132/750ml) -- "straight bourbon" is a legally protected category that specifically excludes blending with other whiskies, so "blend" was the wrong kind. No specific distillery/company identified across sources tried. No peat (bourbon category default).

Confirmed as a genuine Douglas Laing blended Scotch (18 single malts + 4 single grains, tracing to a 1958 cask discovery at the Port of Leith); bottlerSlug set to the already-live douglas-laing row. Peat corrected from none to unknown: sources disagree -- whiskynotes.be's detailed review states only "toasted grains" with no smoke, while lovescotch.com's listing mentions "a hint of smoke" -- kept unknown given the conflict rather than picking a side; no producer-domain (douglaslaing.com) page checked this session to settle it.

Corrected countryCode from XX to GB-SCT and kind from blend to brand. This is a Cameronbridge (Diageo, Fife, Lowland) 12-year-old single grain Scotch, independently bottled by Brave New Spirits (Glasgow) under their "Cask Noir" label -- confirmed on Brave New Spirits' own official site. No peat (grain whisky, essentially always unpeated). The seed's "Brig is Scots dialect" hunch pointed the right direction, though the real story is the Cameronbridge distillery connection rather than a general dialect clue.

Corrected peat from unknown to medium. Nikka's own official site describes Taketsuru Pure Malt's palate as "a light yet layered character, rich with malt and a deep, dense peatiness" with "peat notes" in the finish -- direct producer-domain corroboration, resolving the seed's flagged uncertainty about Yoichi's contribution (the seed's whisky.com fetch had 403'd; nikka.com opened fine this session).

Confirmed countryCode IE and owner: Hibernia Distillers Ltd is a real independent Irish whiskey bonder/bottler based in Innishannon, Co. Cork, founded 2014 by brothers Conor and Alan Hyde -- the same company behind the already-live "Hyde" Irish whiskey brand. "The Forge" itself was not found named on any page opened this session (hiberniadistillers.com remains a placeholder, as the seed noted), so its specific style/peat could not be directly confirmed -- flagged for reviewer; parent company and country are solid.
